description: National Highways has commissioned traffic-speed surveys of the condition of the trunk road network since 2000, under the TRACS (TRAffic-speed Condition Survey) contracts. These surveys utilise image collection and road profile measurements to automatically assess condition. The data is loaded into National Highways' pavement asset management system database (currently P-AMS) where it can be accessed by engineers to assess the condition of lengths of the network and target proposed maintenance schemes. The data is also used at the network level for strategic planning and reporting network performance, for example through its use in the valuation of the road asset and for network level reporting through the Network Pavement Condition (NPC) indicator. Data delivery under the current TRACS contract will end in Q1 of 2027, with the next contract (TRACS6) due to start collection and delivery straightaway after that. TRACS6 will deliver surface condition parameters for the period from April 2027 to March 2032. The TRACS contract specifies detailed performance requirements for the measurements that are to be provided by each survey vehicle used by the survey contractor. A set of accreditation tests are applied to check the suitability of the survey vehicle at the commencement of the survey. On successful completion of these an accreditation certificate is awarded. title: Testing the effect of behavioural interventions on agri-environment scheme optio
buyer: Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs
description: Testing the effect of behavioural interventions on agri-environment scheme option selection This project follows a series of Choice Architecture Tests (CATs) that have been commissioned by Defra's Farming Directorate Behavioural Science and Analytics team. These CATs have tested various interventions in a hypothetical agri-environment scheme application environment to understand their effect on option selection. Key findings include: • CAT 1 : tested the effect of defaults (pre-selected actions) on a hypothetical Sustainable Farming Incentive (SFI) application. Results showed a statistically significant increase in the environmental quality of the agreement generated through defaults compared to the current SFI application design. • CAT 2 : tested the effect of defaults and guided selection on a hypothetical Countryside Stewardship (CS) mid-tier application. title: S30170 Corporate Purchases Decarbonisation Project
description: National Highways has committed to achieving Corporate Carbon Net Zero by 2030. Corporate Purchases contributed approximately 24% of total Corporate Carbon emissions in 2025/26, making it one of the largest sources of organisational emissions and a priority area for decarbonisation. The category includes a range of purchased goods and services, including IT equipment, professional services, employer services, printing and publications, and vehicle procurement. This commission will support the Corporate Carbon Team in identifying, assessing and developing practical opportunities to reduce emissions associated with Corporate Purchases to help support the delivery of the Corporate Carbon Net Zero target by 2030. The work will establish a robust evidence base, engage key stakeholders, assess low carbon procurement opportunities and develop a roadmap to reduce emissions from corporate purchasing activities. The outcomes from this commission will help to improve procurement decision-making, and identify deliverable carbon reduction opportunities, ultimately supporting the achievement of the Corporate Carbon Net Zero 2030 target.

title: S30180 Road Safety Strategy Support
description: This contract is to provide specialist analytical support to strengthen National Highways' approach to achieving its RIS3 road safety targets. Current forecasts indicate a material gap against the ambitious safety outcomes set for the road period, and there is a need for a robust, evidence-based understanding of which interventions will have the greatest impact on reducing casualties and delivering value for money. This commission will bring together and assess the 34 measures contained within the Government's Road Safety Strategy, National Highways' Road to Zero Harm plan, the RIS3 safety programme, and wider stakeholder insight. The objective is to develop a prioritised programme of road safety interventions supported by clear evidence of effectiveness, costs and benefits, including metrics such as cost per KSI prevented. The outputs will provide a critical evidence base for both the delivery of National Highways' own safety programme and engagement with key stakeholders, including DfT, ORR, the Road Safety Strategy Implementation Board and Ministerial Boards. The work will identify gaps in current interventions, assess additional opportunities, evaluate feasibility and effectiveness, and produce a prioritised roadmap of actions and recommendations to support improved safety outcomes across the wider road network.

To support this ambition, ONR intends to commission a comprehensive cultural climate assessment. This requirement aligns with ONR's 2030 Strategy and responds to expectations set out in the UK Government Review of Nuclear Regulation. It is intended to reinforce ONR's cultural foundations and ensure that organisational behaviours, leadership practices and working environments are aligned to strategic objectives. ONR recognises that organisational culture is dynamic and continually evolving. Senior leadership plays a critical role in shaping culture through decision making, behaviours and the environment created across the organisation. As such, cultural improvement must address both: • Structural factors (e.g. governance, organisational design); and • Infrastructure factors (e.g. leadership behaviours, decision making norms, psychological environment). description: Designing and Testing Behaviourally-informed Interventions (Understanding and Addressing Vaccine Uptake and Hesitancy Across Livestock Disease Programmes) The overall aim of this project is to develop an evidence-based understanding of the behavioural and social factors that influence vaccine uptake and hesitancy across a range of animal disease contexts, and to identify opportunities to improve the effectiveness of vaccination as a disease prevention, control and preparedness measure. The project will generate evidence to support the design and implementation of future vaccination policies and programmes, ensuring that behavioural considerations are integrated alongside epidemiological, economic and operational evidence. Specifically, the project seeks to: • Improve understanding of the factors influencing livestock keeper, veterinary and wider stakeholder decisions relating to vaccination. • Identify common and disease-specific drivers, barriers and motivations affecting vaccine uptake, hesitancy and participation in vaccination programmes. • Explore if and how behavioural influences vary across disease contexts, stakeholder groups, sectors and policy settings. • Understand the role of trusted advisers, social networks, markets, supply chains, industry bodies and institutions in shaping vaccination decisions. • Assess behavioural challenges associated with routine preventive vaccination, disease eradication programmes, and emergency vaccination deployed during disease outb…

title: S30168 Feasibility study for developing a quality measure for variable signs and signals settings
description: Timeliness of variable signs and signals (VSS) settings is one of our company's performance indicators. However, we're not able to evaluate the quality of these settings, whether they're appropriate and beneficial for those using our roads. These factors drive customer trust and satisfaction and influence both the Strategic Roads User Survey (SRUS) and Average Delay Key Performance Indicator scores. A KPMG review of our SRUS performance recommended measuring the quality of VSS settings to help identify how we can improve scores. As part of our CSC Business Plan requirement to improve customer experience through better in-journey information we want to commit £83,289.85 of funding (approved through a portfolio business case for VSS improvements by CSC IDC) to carry out a feasibility study to explore the potential of developing a VSS quality measure that would give us sight of how well we're doing in this area. This work is part of the Customer Service Development Group's ongoing portfolio of VSS improvements which seek to improve customer experience and contribute to an increase in customer satisfaction scores. In the 2025-26 reporting year SRUS recorded 71% overall satisfaction and 69% for information on electronic signs. The RIS3 KPI requires SRUS scores to improve year-on-year. description: This procurement seeks to secure a digital post-mortem service in Surrey utilising Computed Tomography (CT) scanning technology. This will support the local authority in meeting its statutory responsibilities under the Coroners and Justice Act 2009 while helping to manage increasing pathology costs and improve service delivery. By providing a non-invasive alternative to traditional post-mortem examinations, CT scanning will significantly reduce the number of invasive procedures undertaken, helping to preserve the dignity of the deceased and improving the experience of bereaved families, particularly those from faith communities with specific cultural or religious requirements. It will also present opportunities for future income generation and operational efficiencies, supporting the long-term sustainability of the Coroner's Service. In doing so, it contributes to the Council's strategic priority of ensuring that no one is left behind by delivering a more compassionate, accessible, and inclusive service for Surrey residents.

The reforms introduce several key improvements to the current framework, including Ofgem's licensing new code managers. The Buyer is turning the high-level design of the new governance framework into detailed licence and code modifications to bring the new framework into effect. title: Qualifying Utilities Dynamic Market (QUDM) for Franchised Bus Services
description: he Qualifying Utilities Dynamic Market (QUDM) will enable the procurement of franchised bus services in support of the Bus Services (Wales) Act 2026. Under the franchising model, the Franchising Authority will determine the services to be provided, service standards and other operational requirements. Contracts for the delivery of franchised bus services will be awarded through competitive procurement processes conducted under the QUDM. The Welsh Ministers are the Franchising Authority for franchised bus services in Wales and contracts awarded under the QUDM will be entered into by the Welsh Ministers in this capacity. Transport for Wales will be responsible for administering and operating the QUDM and will manage procurement procedures and contract administration on behalf of both parties. The QUDM is intended to establish and maintain a pool of qualified suppliers eligible to participate in future procurements for franchised bus services. The QUDM provides a mechanism through which future procurements may be conducted during its lifetime. The contracts to be procured under the QUDM may include the operation of local bus services and associated activities, including service delivery in accordance with contract requirements, operational management, provision of drivers and operational staff, vehicle provision and operation, depot and maintenance arrangements, mobilisation activities, integration with wider network requirements and performance management obligations. title: Qualifying Utilities Dynamic Market (QUDM) for Franchised Bus Services
description: The Qualifying Utilities Dynamic Market (QUDM) will enable the procurement of franchised bus services in support of the Bus Services (Wales) Act 2026. Under the franchising model, the Franchising Authority will determine the services to be provided, service standards and other operational requirements. Contracts for the delivery of franchised bus services will be awarded through competitive procurement processes conducted under the QUDM. The Welsh Ministers are the Franchising Authority for franchised bus services in Wales and contracts awarded under the QUDM will be entered into by the Welsh Ministers in this capacity. Transport for Wales will be responsible for administering and operating the QUDM and will manage procurement procedures and contract administration on behalf of both parties. The QUDM is intended to establish and maintain a pool of qualified suppliers eligible to participate in future procurements for franchised bus services. The QUDM provides a mechanism through which future procurements may be conducted during its lifetime. The contracts to be procured under the QUDM may include the operation of local bus services and associated activities, including service delivery in accordance with contract requirements, operational management, provision of drivers and operational staff, vehicle provision and operation, depot and maintenance arrangements, mobilisation activities, integration with wider network requirements and performance management obligations. description: The Tring Grounds Project delivers a comprehensive enhancement of the museum's external landscape, creating a more accessible, engaging and environmentally diverse visitor experience. The proposals include a reconfigured arrival and parking area, improved pedestrian circulation routes, new accessible pathways through the grounds and woodland, and strengthened connections between key visitor destinations. A geology trail forms a central interpretive element of the scheme, incorporating chalk and stone specimens sourced from local and regional geological contexts to help visitors engage with the area's geological history. Hard landscaping works include new paths, seating, interpretation features, gathering spaces and carefully detailed surface treatments designed to improve accessibility and visitor comfort. Soft landscaping proposals introduce a new orchard, meadow and woodland enhancements, habitat creation, strategic planting and ecological management measures that support biodiversity while enriching the character of the site. description: Hastings Borough Council is seeking a suitably qualified and experienced contractor to undertake the Hastings Castle Priority Works programme. The project comprises conservation and structural repair works to historically significant masonry elements within Hastings Castle, located on Castle Hill Road, Hastings, TN31 3HY. The scope includes the replacement of deteriorated supporting corbels to a historic arch formerly incorporated within one of the church tower walls; stabilisation of the surviving church stair remains through pinning, deep packing and repointing of internal masonry walls; careful dismantling and reconstruction of a section of Victorian wall adjacent to the pathway leading to the public toilets that is currently in poor structural condition; and the removal and replacement of steel plate lintels above the rock-cut dungeon entrance. All works are to be undertaken using appropriate conservation techniques and materials, with due consideration given to preserving the historic character and integrity of the site while improving its long-term stability and safety. Full details of the project and tender requirements are contained within the attached tender pack.

title: London's Violence Reduction Unit - Pan London Tertiary Service

description: About the VRU The London Violence Reduction Unit (VRU), hosted within the Mayor's Office for Policing and Crime (MOPAC), pioneers a partnership-based public health approach to tackling violence rooted in prevention and early intervention. Since 2019, the VRU has invested in over 550,000 targeted interventions for young people across London. Project Background The VRU takes a public health approach to violence reduction, recognising that prevention requires action at different stages. Primary prevention seeks to change the conditions that make violence more likely, strengthening protective factors before violence occurs. Secondary prevention responds when risk or violence is emerging, aiming to interrupt risk and prevent escalation. Tertiary prevention focuses on reducing the harm caused by violence, supporting recovery and reducing the likelihood of further violence. These approaches are complementary, forming part of a wider response to violence and exploitation. Children and young people affected by violence and exploitation can experience complex and interconnected needs, alongside significant barriers to accessing support. These may include safeguarding concerns, trauma, mental health needs, housing instability, disrupted relationships and difficulties accessing education, employment and other opportunities. title: SMRU Seal Flipper Feasibility Study
description: Project Aims The aim of this commission is to undertake a strategic feasibility study assessing the suitability of existing seal telemetry and electronic flipper-tag technologies for supporting future seal monitoring, assessment, and reporting requirements within the UK. The study will review current evidence, technologies, deployment approaches and animal welfare considerations, identify evidence gaps and technical limitations, and evaluate opportunities for future telemetry development. The commission will provide an evidence-based roadmap to support future investment decisions relating to seal telemetry research and technology development. 3. Project Background The Special Committee on Seals (SCOS) has identified robust estimation of UK seal population size and demographic processes as a high research priority. Current monitoring and assessment approaches rely on telemetry-based estimates of haul-out behaviour to support population estimation, particularly for harbour seals. However, existing telemetry evidence remains limited, and uncertainties persist regarding variation in haul-out behaviour, movement ecology, survival, connectivity and demographic parameters. At the same time, significant technological developments have occurred in wildlife telemetry and biologging systems. description: Project Aims To assess the feasibility of applying bioclimate vulnerability assessment approaches to priority marine migratory species within the Caribbean UK Overseas Territories and the Pitcairn Islands. Project Background Climate change is increasingly affecting marine migratory species through changes in sea temperature, ocean productivity, habitat availability, ocean circulation patterns, species interactions and the frequency and intensity of extreme weather events (IPCC, 2022; Martay et al., 2023). description: King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust ("the Trust") is carrying out preliminary market engagement under the Procurement Act 2023 to understand the solutions available for a tissue and cell management system supporting its stem cell transplantation and cellular therapy laboratory services. The Trust currently uses a commercial off-the-shelf tissue and cell management system, in live use since 2023. The infrastructure on which it runs reaches end of support in January 2027, and the Trust is assessing its options for continuity of service from 2027. These include upgrading or migrating the existing solution and adopting an alternative solution. The purpose of this engagement is to establish which providers of this type of system exist in the market, and their level of interest, to help the Trust decide on the most appropriate route to market and timescales. The outcome will inform the Trust's requirements, options appraisal and business case, and the Trust anticipates that it will be followed by a formal procurement. The Trust is seeking solutions that provide end-to-end management and traceability of cellular therapy products, from donor and patient registration through collection, processing, cryopreservation, storage, issue and administration. title: Purchase of Dogs and Associated Services
buyer: The Police and Crime Commissioner for Warwickshire
description: The Police & Crime Commissioner for Warwickshire has awarded a contract for the supply of operational police dogs, including initial training and a guarantee that dogs supplied will achieve the required police licensing standards. The below threshold contract was awarded following approval of an internal exemption. The market for operational police dogs is limited, with only a small number of specialist suppliers capable of sourcing and supplying dogs that meet UK police operational requirements. Each dog must be individually assessed for operational suitability, including temperament, health, trainability, welfare standards and suitability for deployment. Due to the specialist and time-sensitive nature of sourcing suitable police dogs, a competitive procurement process was not considered practical or likely to deliver better value. Value for money is achieved through assessment of each dog against operational requirements, consideration of current market values, and evaluation of health, breeding and welfare standards before purchase. The contract permits the purchase of up to three operational police dogs over a period of up to 18 months, to a maximum value of £27,000 excluding VAT. Supplier details have been withheld under section 94(1)(a) of the Procurement Act 2023 on national security grounds, as disclosure could prejudice operational policing capabilities and increase risks to police dog resources, suppliers and associated facilities.

description: As part of the FSA’s commitment to ensure food is safe and is what it says it is, the FSA undertakes food safety risk assessments which underpin these decisions in line with the internationally recognised ‘Codex Working Principles for Risk Analysis for Food Safety’. A key component of food safety risk assessment is exposure assessment, which estimates the amount of a hazard consumed through the diet. Exposure assessment combines food consumption data with information on the concentrations of substances such as contaminants, food additives or pesticide residues in food to estimate the levels consumers may be exposed to. To conduct UK dietary exposure assessments, the FSA uses consumption data in combination with occurrence data for hazards and other substances in food. UK consumption data is primarily obtained from the UK National Diet and Nutrition Survey (NDNS). The National Diet and Nutrition Survey (NDNS) is a co-funded programme between the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) Office for Health Improvement and Disparities (OHID) and FSA. NDNS is a rolling programme which assesses the diet, nutrient intake and nutritional status of the general population of the UK. Tenders are invited to carry out the recoding of NDNS consumption data to FoodEx2, a standardised system for classifying and describing food.

title: ES RDE 183 - Legacy Soil Phosphorus Mobilisation Review
description: Environment Agency Self-Service Direct Award. Phosphorus (P) is an essential nutrient for crop growth and food production, with agricultural inputs primarily supplied through inorganic fertilisers and organic manures. However, manures are often applied to meet crop nitrogen (N) requirements, which can result in excess P applications and the gradual accumulation of legacy P in soils. This increases the risk of P losses through runoff, erosion, and leaching, contributing to eutrophication of watercourses. As P is frequently the limiting nutrient in freshwater ecosystems, even small releases can cause detrimental environmental impacts, including algal blooms and oxygen depletion. In England, around 55% of rivers and 75% of lakes fail to meet phosphorus standards under the Water Framework Directive.

The objective is to ensure the Laundry Production Equipment is supported by qualified engineers and is fit for the purpose of enabling the Client’s staff to operate the equipment safely, efficiently and reliably. The contractor will be required to survey, design, supply components, install and commission bespoke chimney/flue systems for combustion appliances (mainly natural gas but may on occasion include heating oil and wood pellet fuelled appliances). Each installation will be unique to the individual site. The overall contract may include some maintenance and repair work to existing flue systems. The key standard governing the design and installation of flues for industrial and commercial gas appliances in the UK is IGEM/UP/10 (Installation of flued gas appliances in industrial and commercial premises) IGEM/UP/10 covers the design of flues and exhausts for gas engines exceeding 70 kW net heat input and all gas turbines up to 20 MW.

description: NHS England is undertaking preliminary market engagement to understand how the supplier market could support the future delivery of a Health and Social Care (H&SC) Cyber Supplier and Third Party Risk Management capability. Our ambition is to develop a national capability, available to all health and social care organisations, that delivers a more consistent and scalable approach to managing cyber risk associated with third-party suppliers across health and social care. As part of this work, NHS England is developing a H&SC Cyber Third Party Risk Management Standard, against which relevant suppliers are expected to be assessed. This market engagement will begin with a supplier webinar, followed by a Request for Information (RFI). It gives suppliers an opportunity to help shape this new national capability and the supporting assessment standard. Insights gathered from this exercise will a potential procurement process planned for early to mid-2027. Please note, any figures quoted are early-stage indications only.

title: GOV Voice
description: The Gov Voice programme, led by the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology, is focused on establishing a cross-government, AI-enabled voice capability to modernise how citizens interact with public sector contact services. It centres on deploying generative AI voice technology as a core component of a more integrated and consistent approach to service delivery across organisations. A key aim of the programme is to enhance the overall citizen experience by enabling automated handling of routine enquiries. This approach is designed to reduce wait times, improve accessibility, and provide quicker resolutions for common queries, supporting a more responsive interface with government services. Alongside these user benefits, the programme introduces a reusable and scalable platform that can be adopted across multiple organisations. By providing a centrally assured solution, it reduces duplication of effort and enables a more efficient, coordinated model for delivering voice-based services at scale. Crucially, while led centrally, Gov Voice is intended to be applicable across the whole public sector landscape, enabling adoption by central government departments, local government organisations, and Arm’s Length Bodies (ALBs) to provide a consistent, interoperable voice capability that can operate securely within government environments and scale across multiple services.

title: 5085.SH.JN - Advanced Nano-Mechanical Characterisation System with Integrated Fluorescence
description: The University of Sheffield, supported by the Wolfson Light Microscopy Facility (LMF), is seeking the supply, installation and commissioning of a high-throughput nanoindentation platform for the quantitative mechanical characterisation of biological samples and biomaterials. The instrument will provide a centrally managed research resource supporting investigators from across the Faculties of Health, Science and Engineering, together with external academic and industrial collaborators. The system will enable the measurement of mechanical properties across a broad range of biological specimens including single cells, organoids, tissue sections, extracellular matrices, biomaterials and engineered tissues. The University requires an integrated platform capable of combining high-resolution nanoindentation with optical microscopy and environmental control to permit long-term measurements of live biological samples under physiologically relevant conditions. The instrument must also support high-throughput experimentation using standard multi-well plate formats to facilitate large-scale mechanobiology studies and drug screening. The system shall be supplied as a complete turnkey solution including the nanoindentation platform, integrated optical imaging system, environmental control module, acquisition and analysis software, computer workstation, installation, commissioning and user training. description: Thurrock Council is seeking feedback from organisations with experience in school and community food growing, horticultural education, and community capacity-building to inform the potential future development of this programme. During 2025/26, the Council has successfully delivered a school and community food growing and capacity-building programme across 5 schools and a community setting. The program has supported schools, residents and community groups to develop food growing skills, increase access to green spaces, strengthen community connections, and contribute to wider health and wellbeing outcomes. title: Home At Last Team (HALT) – Housing Support Service
description: The primary objective of this commission is to improve long-term recovery outcomes for people in drug treatment by integrating targeted housing support into the wider recovery framework. This initiative stems from the 10-year Drug Strategy, which allocated £53m to address the significant housing instabilities often cited by individuals entering dependency services. By focusing on the delivery of stable housing, this project seeks to remove a primary barrier to successful treatment completion. Following the success of the HALT project, which commenced in 2021, this specification invites providers to bid to provide a Housing Support Service as part of the Home At Last Team (HALT) to support those with substance use issues into structured treatment and long term sustainable accommodation, which fits into our strategic objective of ‘Increasing Treatment Capacity.’ It will seek to reduce the number of rough sleepers with substance use issues who are not currently engaged in structured treatment, to prevent those within treatment who are at risk of homelessness due to their substance use from becoming homeless, and to offer support (professional and peer) to individuals who are within this cohort.

The cabinet sessions should be held on a weekly basis for two hours, with additional social activities or workshops as required. Collection, transportation, temporary accommodation and welfare support for dogs belonging to vulnerable adults where Adult Social Care has a duty of care under the Care Act 2014, and the owner has become hospitalised, incapacitated, detained, or otherwise unable to care for their dog. title: Opportunity Mapping for Open Mosaic Habitat at the Tees Estuary
description: Open Mosaic Habitat (OMH) is recognised as a high distinctiveness Priority Habitat; which is very difficult to recreate or replace if destroyed. Under S41 NERC Act OMH is protected and Local Planning Authorities require rigorous mitigation if impacted via development. The demand for OMH mitigation opportunities is also intrinsically linked to the planning process and decision-making. This research project will map OMH resource across the Tees Estuary to develop an understanding of the types of OMH across the area, identify areas of OMH not currently mapped and identify whether there have been changes in OMH resource over time. The research project will also collate species records to identify important species using the OMH resource and determine whether there are any characteristic OMH communities. Finally, this work will identify opportunities to maintain and enhance the OMG resource and produce a prioritised list of actions.

description: The Cambridge Genomics Lab provides a comprehensive range of genomic testing for patients with haematological malignancies (haem-onc), with solid cancer, and with rare disease. In the haem-onc setting, we currently utilise a range of molecular techniques including Next-generation sequencing, quantitative PCR, and fragment analysis to identify and monitor clinically significant genomic alterations. However, there is an increasing requirement for high sensitivity, quantitative molecular testing both to support diagnosis and for disease monitoring / assessment of therapeutic response. We are therefore looking to procure a Digital / Digital Droplet (dPCR / ddPCR) system to complement the laboratory’s existing molecular testing capabilities. This would also intend to facilitate the consolidation of multiple existing assays and methodologies onto a single technology platform.

description: The Perinatal Pathology Transport service is required to replace ad hoc transport arrangements with a single, and coordinated national service. Journeys are currently arranged locally, often through funeral directors, with variation in cost and no overall control of availability, or quality. Workforce shortages and uneven capacity is increasing the need for deceased babies to be transferred between pathology centres for post mortem examinations. There are currently no standards for the current local arrangements to follow or transport-specific requirements in place. This creates an avoidable risk of loss of tissue integrity and delayed post-mortem results. A pre-market engagement shall be conducted on Wed 2nd Dec from 10am to help identify suppliers who are willing to provide suggestions on service improvements and efficiencies, whilst respecting and retaining the dignity of the deceased.

title: Well Wave Plus: (Open Access and Equity)
description: The Well Wave Plus: Open Access and Equity contract will complement and enhance the existing Well Wave service. Well Wave is a city wide, universal offer for young people aged 13-24, overseen by the Leeds City Council Public Health team. Trained workers offer confidential, non-clinical relationships and sexual health support, where young people can explore ideas, build skills and access free condom products, lubricant, and pregnancy testing, plus STI self-screening kits. These drop-in services are located within organisations where young people already attend. This contract will enhance current provision by introducing specialist, dedicated Well Wave Plus workers with the skills to engage and appropriately support most at risk, least well-supported and seldom seen young people aged 13-24 years old. Currently, most workers trained to deliver Well Wave provide the service voluntarily within their substantive roles (e.g. in youth clubs or educational settings). Under this contract, dedicated workers will be employed solely to deliver and promote Well Wave services, without constraints on location or caseload. These workers will focus on ensuring equity of access for seldom seen, marginalised or under pressure young people by developing and delivering flexible, accessible, and culturally sensitive Well Wave outreach in appropriate community setting

description: This notice relates to the procurement of the replacement of the Social Enterprise Dynamic Purchasing System (SEDPS) which expires on 14th August 2028. National Highways established SEDPS in 2023 to improve access to public sector contracting opportunities for VCSEs and other organisations that reinvest their surpluses to deliver social value. SEDPS was created to make public procurement more accessible by reducing barriers to entry and creating a simpler route to market for National Highways, its supply chain, and other public sector organisations. title: Multiple Disadvantage and Housing Support Alliance
suppliers: Places for People Living Plus; Roundabout Ltd; Shelter
description: The Multiple Disadvantage and Housing Support Service, will work in a streamlined and holistic manner across the area of Sheffield. It will provide holistic and multi-faceted floating support to people who experience multiple disadvantage – officially defined as a co-morbidity of homelessness/housing insecurity, mental health needs, substance use, involvement with the criminal justice system and domestic abuse – often further compounded by additional factors such as trauma, poverty, discrimination and stigma. The integrated service will aim to prevent and tackle multiple disadvantage, whilst recognising the intersectionality and compounding impact of the areas of need outlined above. The service will build on local learning from the Changing Futures programme and aligns with the city’s strategy Coordination from Complexity (2025–2030), consultation findings, and the Alliance Commissioning Vision. It will provide a clear, equitable and trauma-informed offer across three pathways: (1) Young People aged 16–25 (2) Adults aged 25+ (3) Recovery and Co-production (all ages). This contract is being awarded as an alliance contract, which means the Council expects tender responses to be submitted on behalf of groups of suppliers that are able collectively to deliver the Services.

title: Refresh of Councillor Handbook on Libraries
cpv_description: Research and development services and related consultancy services
description: The context in which libraries operate has moved on since our Councillor handbook was first published in 2017. The planned refresh of the publication aims to provide councillors – primarily those with portfolio responsibility for library services – with a guide that outlines the key statutory requirements for delivering the service, opportunities to design and prepare the service for future changes, and options for maximising the service’s impact for local residents. This will include case studies of interesting and effective practice. Where relevant, sections of the existing handbook may be retained and incorporated into the refreshed guide. Your Quotation should give an indicative and high level outline of where you think change is required, and what could be usefully retained. The guide aims to support practical advocacy for library services, providing prompts or key questions to help readers assemble evidence and make the case for their services. Suppliers should propose the most useful format to do this in their submission. The guide should aim to support councillors to make connections with policy objectives across a range of council outcomes, including neighbourhood health, early years and skills, economic growth in every postcode, and high street regeneration. The guide will not be expected to deal with all of these in depth but can signpost to existing information where it exists,

description: Mill Gate transformation is a catalyst project that will reposition the shopping centre and its surroundings as a more connected, attractive and commercially resilient town-centre destination. Building on the aspirations of the Mill Gate Regeneration Framework, the proposals focus on opening up the existing mall environment, creating new public spaces, improving pedestrian connectivity and establishing development-ready plots for future phases of regeneration. The works are centred around three key areas: The Square, Minden & Market Parade and Union Square. Collectively, they involve selective demolition, public realm reconstruction, alterations to existing buildings and canopies, refurbishment of retained frontages, servicing and highways modifications, landscaping, lighting, drainage and infrastructure works. The objective is not simply to improve the physical environment, but to reconnect Mill Gate with Bury Market, the Interchange, The Rock and surrounding town-centre destinations whilst supporting future mixed-use regeneration. Contractors should anticipate a complex town-centre regeneration project delivered within a live trading environment, requiring careful phasing, stakeholder coordination, maintenance of pedestrian access and ongoing operation of businesses, markets and servicing functions throughout the construction period.

description: Transport for London (TfL)'s current Visitor Centre commercial ticketing and visitor services contracts are due to expire in April 2027. TfL is taking this opportunity to engage with the market and explore how its Visitor Centres can evolve to meet the changing needs of customers, visitors and commercial partners. Through this engagement, TfL wishes to understand emerging customer trends, innovative products and services, technology solutions, and commercial delivery models that could support the future Visitor Centre proposition beyond 2027. London remains one of the world's leading visitor destinations and continues to play a central role in the UK's visitor economy. Visitor expectations are evolving, with customers increasingly seeking personalised recommendations, seamless digital experiences, greater flexibility and convenient access to attractions, entertainment and travel products. TfL welcomes views from attractions, cultural and entertainment organisations, tour and experience providers, ticketing and technology suppliers, destination management organisations, aggregators, marketplaces and other organisations that can help shape the next generation of visitor experiences. Through this early market engagement, TfL aims to better understand how future partnerships could create value for customers, partners and TfL alike, while supporting the development of a commercially sustainable and customer-focused Visitor Centre proposition.

Thermal vacuum (TVAC) chambers require high-vacuum capability (typically ≤ 1×10−5 hPa), wide-range temperature cycling (often -190 °C to +150°C or higher), and precise thermal control (control surface stability in the range ±0.1 °C/min), usually achieved via liquid nitrogen, shrouds and heating platens. title: Preliminary Market Engagement: Smart Meter Energy Data for Data Linkage Study

description: Public Health Wales (PHW) is undertaking a study, commissioned by Welsh Government, to quantify the energy costs of people with long-term health conditions and disabilities across Wales, specifically those that result in unavoidably high energy use due to long-term health conditions, disability or care needs (hereafter long-term health conditions, LTCs). The study will have two stages: • Stage one, conducted in-house, will involve PHW mapping LTCs which require high energy use and the type of energy need (e.g. heating, cooling, powering equipment) based on existing evidence. It will also map the support available for such households. • Stage two will involve procurement and draw on the LTCs identified in stage one. A data-linkage study will quantify energy costs and provide more granular data on households with high energy use related to LTCs. This may include, but is not limited to, the increased energy cost or (where not available) energy consumption in households with LTCs and associated with each LTC (compared to those without LTCs), the number of individuals with each LTC, and their geographical distribution in Wales. To enable the delivery of stage two and specifically the quantification of increased energy cost or consumption in households with LTCs, PHW plan to procure an energy data consultancy to obtain household-level smart meter energy cost data or, where billing information is not available, energy consumption data.

description: Mill Gate transformation is a catalyst project that will reposition the shopping centre and its surroundings as a more connected, attractive and commercially resilient town-centre destination. The works are centred around three key areas: The Square, Minden & Market Parade and Union Square. Collectively, they involve selective demolition, public realm reconstruction, alterations to existing buildings and canopies, refurbishment of retained frontages, servicing and highways modifications, landscaping, lighting, drainage and infrastructure works. description: Recent reviews of the UK utility sectors, including the Independent Water Commission’s (Cunliffe) Report, have highlighted the importance of robust asset management, engineering assurance and asset health oversight in supporting the resilience of critical infrastructure. In response, Ofgem is enhancing its approach to asset assurance across the gas and electricity sectors through the establishment of the Asset Health Inspectorate (AHI). The AHI will undertake a programme of audits and inspections to assess the effectiveness of asset management systems, governance arrangements and maintenance practices operated by regulated network companies. This includes reviewing asset management processes, maintenance records and the condition of assets in the field, as well as investigating significant network incidents where appropriate. To support this work, Ofgem is developing specialist engineering and asset management capability across its workforce. The Institute of Asset Management (IAM) Certificate qualification has been identified as a key foundation-level training programme to equip staff with a practical understanding of asset management principles, asset lifecycle management, risk-based decision making and recognised industry good practice. title: Provision of Consultancy Services for the Development of a Hillingdon Circus Junction Movement and Public Realm Strategy
description: Hillingdon Circus is strategically located at the junction of Long Lane and the A40 Western Avenue, with Hillingdon Underground Station to the north and the Master Brewer development site occupying the land to the east of Long Lane, between the A40 and Freezeland Way. The Circus functions as an important multimodal gateway, connecting strategic movement along the A40 with Underground, bus and coach services, alongside local walking and cycling routes. Long Lane forms an important north-south corridor, linking Ickenham and areas to the north of the A40 with Hillingdon, Uxbridge Road and neighbourhoods to the south, while also connecting local shops, schools and community facilities. However, this strong strategic connectivity is accompanied by highway-dominated infrastructure and complex traffic movements that create significant local severance. Wide carriageways, slip roads, level changes and junction arrangements weaken connections between the station, local centre, and surrounding residential areas. Pedestrian movement is often indirect and constrained by complex crossings, level changes and highway infrastructure, while parts of the public realm suffer from poor legibility, limited greenery and anti-social behaviour, particularly around underpasses and poorly overlooked spaces. title: Best Start Family Hubs
description: The national Best Start Family Hubs and Healthy Babies programme sets a refreshed direction for family and health support from April 2026 to March 2029. It builds on the learning from Sure Start, Family Hubs and Start for Life, with a clear expectation that local areas bring together health, education, early years, parenting and community support so that families can access help earlier, more easily and in places they already know and trust. The programme places strong emphasis on early identification, prevention and reducing inequalities, particularly during pregnancy and the early years when the foundations for lifelong health, learning and development are laid. Best Start Family Hubs should provide a welcoming and inclusive front door for families, supported by a wider network of linked local services and outreach locations, so that families can receive the right support at the right time and are not left to navigate services on their own. The updated national guidance describes Best Start Family Hubs as a key part of the Government's wider Best Start in Life strategy, supporting the ambition for more children to achieve a good level of development by age five. The model remains universal and open to families from conception to age 19, or up to 25 for young people with special educational needs and disabilities, while prioritising support for families with babies and young children. title: Provision of Consultancy Services for the Development of a Hillingdon Circus Junction Movement and Public Realm Strategy
description: Hillingdon Circus is strategically located at the junction of Long Lane and the A40 Western Avenue, with Hillingdon Underground Station to the north and the Master Brewer development site occupying the land to the east of Long Lane, between the A40 and Freezeland Way. The Circus functions as an important multimodal gateway, connecting strategic movement along the A40 with Underground, bus and coach services, alongside local walking and cycling routes. Long Lane forms an important north-south corridor, linking Ickenham and areas to the north of the A40 with Hillingdon, Uxbridge Road and neighbourhoods to the south, while also connecting local shops, schools and community facilities. However, this strong strategic connectivity is accompanied by highway-dominated infrastructure and complex traffic movements that create significant local severance. Wide carriageways, slip roads, level changes and junction arrangements weaken connections between the station, local centre, and surrounding residential areas. Pedestrian movement is often indirect and constrained by complex crossings, level changes and highway infrastructure, while parts of the public realm suffer from poor legibility, limited greenery and anti-social behaviour, particularly around underpasses and poorly overlooked spaces. title: Hidden Critical Elements Condition Assessment Solutions
cpv_description: Technical inspection services of engineering structures
description: Network Rail is undertaking preliminary market engagement to explore specialist solutions for assessing the condition of Hidden Critical Elements (HCEs) within existing railway structures. The requirement is focused on methods capable of establishing and evidencing the condition and deterioration of concealed structural elements, rather than solely locating them. Solutions may be non intrusive or hybrid and should provide interpretable results covering condition, coverage, confidence and limitations, supported by appropriate validation against known condition or targeted intrusive examination. The engagement will explore technical capability, safe deployment within the operational railway, access and possession requirements, site duration, scalability, supplier capacity, unit costs and whole life affordability. It will also help Network Rail refine its requirements, validation approach and future procurement strategy. Any subsequent trial or procurement will be subject to appropriate technical, safety, assurance, commercial and governance approvals, and participation in this engagement does not constitute a commitment by Network Rail to procure a solution.

title: C0193 - AI Programme - Learning & Evaluation
description: Artificial intelligence (AI) is developing quickly and is already affecting how communities, public services and civil society organisations operate. It brings opportunities to improve services, reduce administrative pressure and develop new approaches to community needs. It also presents risks relating to exclusion, bias, environmental sustainability and the concentration of power. The Fund wants communities and civil society organisations to play an active role in shaping how AI is developed and used. The Fund has approved AI-related funding designed to build community agency, support responsible adoption and generate practical learning for the Fund and the wider sector. The Fund’s AI-related funding portfolio currently includes three strands: • AI capacity-building uplifts in England and Scotland; • Community-Powered AI grants; and • the Pulse Network. The three strands, detailed in section 2 below, differ in their scale, purpose and delivery model. The AI Capacity Building Uplifts are being wholly funded and delivered by the National Lottery Community Fund. The Community-Powered AI and Pulse Network strands are being delivered through a collaboration between The National Lottery Community Fund, UK Community Foundations (UKCF) and CAST. UKCF is the lead partner for the Community-Powered AI and Pulse Network strands. title: CN250565 - Community Wellbeing Service for Older People, Physical Disability and Dementia
description: The Community Wellbeing Service for Older People, Physical Disability and Dementia aims to help people take a proactive approach to their health and wellbeing, increase independence, and prevent, reduce or delay the need for statutory services. This is achieved via support which includes, but is not limited to: peer groups, physical activities, providing information (e.g. about support in the local community and how to manage money and benefits), supporting people to live safely in their own home, and maintaining and adapting an individual’s home to their needs with low level trusted assessor equipment. These services form part of Kent County Council’s (KCC) wider prevention offer and contributes to reducing demand for statutory services by intervening early and supporting people to manage their wellbeing before needs escalate. The proposed Community Wellbeing Service for Older People, Physical Disability and Dementia will replace the existing Wellbeing Services in the Community contracts, which are commissioned separately for older people, people with dementia, and people with physical disabilities through a range of Voluntary Community Sector Enterprise (VCSE) partners. The proposed contracts will provide services for •Older People (55+) •People with dementia and their families •People with a physical disability

title: London's Violence Reduction Unit - Pan London Tertiary Service

description: About the VRU The London Violence Reduction Unit (VRU), hosted within the Mayor's Office for Policing and Crime (MOPAC), pioneers a partnership-based public health approach to tackling violence rooted in prevention and early intervention. Since 2019, the VRU has invested in over 550,000 targeted interventions for young people across London. Project Background The VRU takes a public health approach to violence reduction, recognising that prevention requires action at different stages. Primary prevention seeks to change the conditions that make violence more likely, strengthening protective factors before violence occurs. Secondary prevention responds when risk or violence is emerging, aiming to interrupt risk and prevent escalation. Tertiary prevention focuses on reducing the harm caused by violence, supporting recovery and reducing the likelihood of further violence. These approaches are complementary, forming part of a wider response to violence and exploitation. Children and young people affected by violence and exploitation can experience complex and interconnected needs, alongside significant barriers to accessing support. description: The appointment of an independent person under the Local Government Pension Scheme (LGPS) relating to the Staffordshire Pension Fund. This appointment refers to The Local Government Pension Scheme (Amendment) (Governance) Regulations 2026, which introduces amendments to the Local Government Pension Scheme Regulations 2013. New Regulation 53A(5) provides that, where an administering authority delegates its functions or part of its functions under the 2013 Regulations to a committee, sub committee or an officer, it must appoint an independent person to support the discharge of functions in relation to the Scheme including investment strategy, governance and administration. Staffordshire County Council in its capacity as the administering authority of the Fund delegates relevant functions to the Pensions Committee and is therefore required to make such an appointment.

description: Please provide a detailed description of the notice you are adding: The final date and time for the submission of bids is Wednesday, 14th October 2026 at 11:00 DO NOT apply directly to the buyer. Brief Description of Requirement It is broadly recognised that physical climate risk and related nature dependencies can pose risks to economic and financial stability. Governments and regulators in the UK and internationally have recognised this and continue to take action to address underlying vulnerabilities and support wider systemic resilience. Notwithstanding the clear need for accelerated global action, there remains significant uncertainties in appraising the future economic and financial implications of physical risk meaning market practices, government policy and regulation, may not be optimised (within the bounds of wider limitations and mandates) to align with climate-resilient pathways. Climate scenario analysis is a key tool to inform approaches to climate risk management. But due to the complexity and heterogeneity of climate risk, academic and industry evidence has highlighted that current mainstream scenarios – whilst highly sophisticated – may not capture all potential physical risk due to limited data availability and modelling constraints. buyer: NHS HAMPSHIRE AND THE ISLE OF WIGHT INTEGRATED CARE BOARD
description: The service aims to provide high-quality support for carers that is accessible, equitable and responsive to the needs of our local Isle of Wight population. The service will be delivered to carers resident on the Isle of Wight, ensuring timely access to information, advice, and guidance during a cared-for person's acute hospital admission-whether for physical or mental health needs. Its purpose is to improve outcomes, experiences, and long-term resilience, helping individuals remain in their chosen place of residence for longer, reducing reliance on statutory services, and delaying or preventing permanent admission to residential care. The provider will offer care that is standardised, transparent and coordinated, enabling carers to feel supported throughout the acute stay of their cared for individual, receive optimal interventions and support the first time, and experience improved independence and ability to remain in or return to their caring responsibilities. A collaborative approach involving all stakeholders in the health and social care pathway will be essential to ensure equitable outcomes and a positive experience for both carers and cared for individuals.

description: This procurement is for a Contract, which is an exempted contract under s 3(6) and Schedule 2, Part 2 (Subject-matter exempted contracts), paragraph 22 (Research and Development Services) of the Procurement Act 2023 (the 'Act'). Exempted contracts are not public contracts as defined in s3 of the Act and therefore are not required to be procured in accordance with the provisions of the Act that relate to a covered procurement. For this procurement the Authority has operated a transparent competition process, to which any potential supplier was able to respond. In doing so the procurement process has reflected processes and requirements set out in the Act in relation to covered procurements, or elements thereof. This commitment to transparency includes the publication of this notice, for information, on Find a Tender. The UK Active Debris Removal Phase 3 Research and Development Service (ADR Mission) is a UK national project that aims to support the In-Orbit Servicing and Manufacturing ("ISAM") and Sustainability priorities set out in the UK Space Agency's Corporate Plan as well as the National Space Strategy (NSS) ambitions to lead the global effort to make space more sustainable. The ADR Mission requires the safe capture and subsequent removal of two UK-licensed defunct satellites in the congested LEO region (Client Satellites) by the Servicer Satellite. Through this Procurement, the Authority has selected one Supplier to deliver the UK ADR Mission.

title: Gambling Insights
cpv_description: Social research services; Health and social work services
description: Stockton-on-Tees Borough Council (SBC) is seeking expressions of interest (EOI) from suitably experienced providers to undertake insight research exploring gambling-related harms within Stockton-on-Tees. This work will complement a rapid Health Needs Assessment (HNA) and its associated recommendations, providing a more detailed understanding of local experiences, perceptions and impacts. The purpose of the project is to develop a deeper understanding of the nature, extent and impact of gambling-related harms across the borough, including the experiences of affected individuals, families, communities and key stakeholders. The findings will strengthen the local evidence base, enhance understanding of the scale and impact of gambling-related harms in Stockton-on-Tees, and inform future prevention, early intervention and support approaches. The insights generated will support future prevention and commissioning activity, helping to ensure that interventions are accessible, responsive to local need, and appropriately targeted.

description: This commission will establish a technically credible and decision-ready basis for the future application of rapid response flood risk designation across England. The supplier will review the purpose, definition and operational use of the current Rapid Response Catchment approach, drawing on Environment Agency stakeholder input from flood resilience, forecasting, incident management and flood risk teams. The work will define the physical and operational characteristics of rapid response flood risk, identify communities at risk, and develop a purpose statement, glossary, decision-support matrix, conceptual model(s), and principles for classification and spatial representation. In parallel, the supplier will review relevant national and local datasets, assess their suitability, consistency, transparency and maintainability, and identify data gaps. The commission will also produce a strategic plan for potential national implementation, including technical governance, ownership and maintenance arrangements, an indicative programme and cost range, implementation risks, and a decision paper. Outputs will comprise technical reports, a dataset catalogue, an implementation programme and risk register.

title: Thermal Conductivity Measurement System
cpv_description: Machines and apparatus for testing and measuring
procedure: Award procedure without prior publication of a call for competition
description: Market research has established that the technical requirements for these systems can only be met by Merrow Scientific Ltd, acting as the UK partner for Linseis Messgeräte GmbH. Both internal research activity and external customers require measurement across the full temperature range of −50°C to 1,000°C using xenon flash technology. Linseis is the only manufacturer identified that can deliver this range. The system can also achieve high vacuum levels at sub-ambient temperatures. This is particularly important for work down to −50°C, where it allows residual moisture to be effectively removed from the chamber. It also gives far greater control over the gas atmosphere surrounding the sample, supporting more consistent and reproducible measurement conditions. The DSC offers very rapid heating rates and accurate heat capacity measurement, which is required to complement the LFA measurements. Its optical access allows the sample to be observed visually and opens the potential for spectroscopic analysis, such as Raman. This visual observation also strengthens the educational value of the technique. In addition, the DSC uses a replaceable chip, providing a cost-effective and sustainable means of maintaining reliable operation. This is critical for both the internal research community and external customers.

title: ITT 70/2026 - Mourne Gullion Landscape Connections Baseline Environmental Surveys Reporting
buyer: Newry Mourne and Down District Council
description: Newry, Mourne and Down District Council (The Council) is inviting tenders from suitably experienced suppliers to undertake the Mourne Gullion Landscape Connections Baseline Environmental Surveys and Reporting. This requires a suitably qualified and experienced environmental consultancy to undertake baseline environmental surveys across the Mourne and Ring of Gullion Areas of Outstanding Natural Beauty (AONBs). The commission shall comprise a combination of desktop data analysis, habitat mapping, field-based habitat survey and condition assessment, LiDAR and vegetation analysis, and drone surveys of selected river corridors. The outputs shall be delivered in a Geographic Information System (GIS) compatible format and provide a comprehensive baseline dataset to support future nature recovery planning, works, and monitoring programmes. The purpose of the commission is to establish a robust, evidence-based environmental baseline against which future changes in habitat extent, habitat condition, vegetation structure, river corridor condition and biodiversity enhancement initiatives can be measured and monitored as part of the Mourne Gullion Landscape Connections project.

title: Sustainable Aviation Fuel Revenue Certainty Mechanism Delivery Partner
description: DfT is in the process of developing a Revenue Certainty Mechanism (RCM) for First-of-a-Kind (FOAK) Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) projects in the UK. The RCM is time-limited and industry-funded intervention, aiming to de-risk SAF projects by offering a Guaranteed Strike Price (GSP) for each unit of SAF produced. This aims to reduce the cost of capital and unlock Final Investment Decisions (FID) to operationalise projects that can support demand driven by the Government’s SAF Mandate. The SAF Mandate secures the demand for SAF by obligating the supply of an increasing amount of SAF in the overall UK aviation fuel mix and incentivising SAF supply through the award of tradeable certificates with a cash value. The overarching goal of the RCM and SAF Mandate is to achieve decarbonisation in the aviation sector, supporting the Government’s ambition to become a Clean Energy Superpower.

description: Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust has awarded a contract for the supply of an EmbryoScope+ time-lapse embryo incubator for use within the Jessop Fertility Unit. The contract was awarded to replace an existing EmbryoScope+ unit that had sustained irreparable damage and could no longer be utilised clinically. Time-lapse embryo incubators are essential to the delivery of IVF services, enabling continuous monitoring of embryo development through automated image capture without the need to remove embryos from the controlled incubator environment. The replacement equipment will maintain service continuity, clinical capacity and patient care within the IVF laboratory. The existing VTH server and storage infrastructure remain fully operational and compatible with the replacement unit; therefore, only the incubator was included within the scope of this procurement. description: About the VRU The London Violence Reduction Unit (VRU), hosted within the Mayor's Office for Policing and Crime (MOPAC), pioneers a partnership-based public health approach to tackling violence rooted in prevention and early intervention. Since 2019, the VRU has invested in over 550,000 targeted interventions for young people across London. Project Background The VRU takes a public health approach to violence reduction, recognising that prevention requires action at different stages. Primary prevention seeks to change the conditions that make violence more likely, strengthening protective factors before violence occurs. Secondary prevention responds when risk or violence is emerging, aiming to interrupt risk and prevent escalation. Tertiary prevention focuses on reducing the harm caused by violence, supporting recovery and reducing the likelihood of further violence. These approaches are complementary, forming part of a wider response to violence and exploitation. This will be conducted via a quotation process. Stalking is a pattern of repeated, unwanted behaviour. Anyone can be a stalker, and anyone can be a victim. There is no legal definition in the UK for stalking, but stalking is a criminal offence under the Protection of Harassment Act 1997 (Section 2A and 4A). The FOUR acronym: Fixated, Obsessive, Unwanted and Repeated highlights the personal fixation that characterises stalking and helps to distinguish it from harassment. The limited research available on Stalking and young people evidences young people’s difficulty in identifying and recognising stalking. Research demonstrates that the removal of personal boundaries through shared online spaces are contributing to young people’s difficulties in identifying stalking behaviours. There is a particular difficulty amongst young people in identifying when bulling ends and stalking begins. Research on the experience of those who support young victims of stalking found that the normalisation sharing personal information and being watched increasing the risk to victims and causing them to not identify worrying behaviours. description: This notice relates to the first re-opening of the Social Impact Framework. The EoECPH Social Impact Framework aims to provide a structured, compliant procurement route for services that deliver social betterment and impact, aligning with NHS and government priorities such as reducing inequalities, improving community well-being, and enhancing sustainability. This Framework will support NHS trusts and Integrated Care Boards (ICBs) in procuring high-quality services that address key social challenges, including homelessness, financial inclusion, employment support, offender rehabilitation, and community integration. While Voluntary, Community, and Social Enterprises (VCSEs) and SMEs currently deliver many of these services, the Framework is open to all eligible suppliers, ensuring full compliance with the Procurement Act 2023. The Framework will: • Simplify access to suppliers delivering social impact services. • Ensure compliance under the Procurement Act 2023. • Improve efficiency by providing a pre-qualified list of suppliers. • Drive social and economic development. This open Framework will be subject to the Light Touch Regime under the Procurement Act 2023. Local Plans are increasingly expected to actively contribute to nature recovery. The diagnostic will help local planning authorities understand how effectively their nature-recovery ambitions and relevant evidence are reflected through their Local Plan, including the spatial strategy, site allocations, infrastructure planning and development policies. It will also consider how Local Nature Recovery Strategies (LNRS) and other relevant environmental evidence inform plan-making and how engagement with Natural England has supported Local Plan preparation. description: In 2017, Transport for London (TfL) awarded a framework agreement for the delivery of Rapid Electric Vehicle Charge Points (EVCPs). description: Bolton Metropolitan Borough Council "The Authority" requires provision for Section 19 Alternative Provision services. Section 19 of the Education act 1996 is the statutory duty to provide suitable education for all children and young people of compulsory school age who cannot access mainstream school places. This includes, permanently excluded pupils, and pupils who, because of illness or other reasons, cannot attend mainstream. Bolton Council determine the number of high needs places required each year and submits the figures to the DfE by December 5th for the following academic year. These are finalised and published in February before September term starts. This process should reflect planned and predicted changes for the following academic year, so that schools and colleges receive an appropriate level of core funding, that enables them to make the special provision that is to be commissioned, particularly any expansion of that provision. The Authority ran an Open Tender Process for a 1-year contract for the Academic year 2027 to 2028 provision, as the Provider needs to be in place before November 2026 to be able to submit to the DfE on time. title: 0358 Nursery Bridge Structural Bearing Replacement Scheme 2026
description: Nursery Bridge is a single span simply supported steel composite structure, which carries Atherleigh Way (A579), over Pennington Brook, in Leigh. The deck consists of a reinforced concrete deck slab, which is composite with 11 914x419x343 UB’s, spaced at 1.350m centres. The steel beams are supported on bearings and reinforced concrete plinths, on top of brick faced, reinforced concrete full height abutments. The bearings at the north end of the structure are rocker bearings which are to be replaced under this contract. Records suggest there is an existing United Utilities 160mm mains water supply pipe in the East verge and a 33kV electricity northwest cable in the west verge and northbound carriageway although this is noted to be out of commission. The reconstruction works briefly comprise: - Excavation to topsoil above abutment toe - Sequenced propping of the structure during overnight road closure - Hydro-demolition of existing bearing plinths - Re-casting of bearing plinths - Installation of new bearings - Installation of new asphaltic plug joint - Installation and removal of traffic management The Contractor to provide all necessary transport, tools, access equipment, appropriate welfare, water disposal and clearance on completion in order to carry out the works effectively. We require full risk assessments and method statements (RAMS) before commencement. The sites will be under control of CDM 2015.

title: UKRI-7477 2026 SciVal and Scopus renewal UKRI
description: This is a transparency notice to inform the market that UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) intends to award a contract to Elsevier for the continued provision of access to its Scopus and SciVal products. Scopus provides access to a bibliometric database of research publications, enabling UKRI to explore and analyse research outputs at individual, institutional and portfolio levels. SciVal builds on the underlying Scopus data, providing analytical tools to support research performance analysis, benchmarking, topic clustering and the assessment of research impact. The products are used by UKRI's analysis teams to support programme and portfolio evaluations, assess research productivity, benchmark research performance and inform strategic decision-making, including evidence for spending reviews. The continued provision of these services is required to maintain established datasets, analytical methodologies, historical benchmarks and consistency across UKRI's research analysis and evaluation activities. UKRI intends to make the award by direct award under Section 41(1) and Schedule 5, paragraph 6 of the Procurement Act 2023, on the grounds of an absence of competition for technical reasons and the absence of reasonable alternatives.

title: Local Wildlife Sites and 30by30
buyer: The West of England Combined Authority
description: There are approximately 845 SNCIs within the West of England region (including two located entirely within the Severn Estuary, which we are anticipating to be out of scope for this project), spread across four local authorities; Bristol City Council (BCC), Bath & North East Somerset Council (BANES), North Somerset Council (NSC) and South Gloucestershire Council (SGC). SNCIs are a key part of the West of England's ecological network, covering approximately 13% of the region's land area and making a significant contribution to Local Nature Recovery Strategy (LNRS) priorities and regional 30by30 aspirations. However, most sites lack up-to-date survey and monitoring data, limiting understanding of their condition, management needs, eligibility for Defra 30by30 criteria, and value for nature recovery. The West of England Combined Authority seeks to procure ecological surveys which provide this data across approximately 850 sites within the West of England over a three-year period. The contract would also include the production of management plans for these sites.

description: The GB rail industry is at a critical point in its transition to digital train control. We are committed to ETCS to deliver a safer, more reliable, higher-performing and affordable railway. However, recent GB and European onboard fitment schemes have highlighted that the cost and pace of delivery must improve significantly if we are to deliver at the scale required to unlock the benefits at a system level. The service will contribute to the implementation of the Scottish Government Breastfeeding and Infant Feeding Strategic Framework and NHS GGC's Infant Feeding Policy and will support the delivery and sustainability of UNICEF UK Baby Friendly standards. The successful provider will work in partnership with NHS GGC, Health and Social Care Partnerships (HSCPs), maternity, neonatal, health visiting, Family Nurse Partnership (FNP) and other relevant services to provide an integrated breastfeeding support offer across NHS GGC. The service will follow and develop the existing model of community breastfeeding peer support, including the delivery of breastfeeding/infant-feeding support groups, recruitment and training of peer volunteers and targeted engagement with communities experiencing inequalities.

description: NHS GGC recognises the important contribution that third-sector organisations can make through the provision of breastfeeding peer support. Peer support offers families access to people with relevant lived experience who can provide practical, social and emotional support, complementing the clinical and professional support provided by NHS services. The service will contribute to the implementation of the Scottish Government Breastfeeding and Infant Feeding Strategic Framework and NHS GGC's Infant Feeding Policy and will support the delivery and sustainability of UNICEF UK Baby Friendly standards. The successful provider will work in partnership with NHS GGC, Health and Social Care Partnerships (HSCPs), maternity, neonatal, health visiting, Family Nurse Partnership (FNP) and other relevant services to provide an integrated breastfeeding support offer across NHS GGC. The service will follow and develop the existing model of community breastfeeding peer support, including the delivery of breastfeeding/infant-feeding support groups, recruitment and training of peer volunteers and targeted engagement with communities experiencing inequalities.
