description: 1. As part of wider work to develop a long term policy framework to replace the Scottish Governmentâs existing air quality strategy Cleaner Air for Scotland 2 (CAFS2), which expires at the end of 2026, air quality objectives in Scotland are being reviewed. Although all current objectives are being met across the country, an increasing body of research shows that air pollution, even at the low levels currently experienced in much of Scotland, continues to harm human health across all life stages and in a multitude of different ways. 2. The Scottish Governmentâs aim is to propose challenging but achievable new objectives, thereby delivering further benefits for human health. In the short term, we wish to assess the feasibility of matching or where possible going further than the air quality targets for nitrogen dioxide and fine particulate matter, two pollutants of concern for human health, which are set out in the EU Directive 2024/2881 on ambient air quality and cleaner air for Europe and are to be achieved by 2030. In the medium to longer term (i.e. the 10-15 years after 2030), we wish to consider the feasibility of going beyond the EU targets and working towards the considerably more stringent World Health Organisation guidelines, which were updated in 2021. Any proposals will be subject to public consultation and approval by Ministers prior to being adopted. 3. In the medium to longer term (i.e. the 10-15 years after 2030), we wish to consider the feasibility of going beyond the EU targets and working towards the considerably more stringent World Health Organisation guidelines, which were updated in 2021. title: PROC 26-3490 Greenock Phase 1 - Ben Lomond View (BLV) refurbishment
description: The Authority wishes to appoint a contractor to deliver the works package for the refurbishment of Ben Lomond View, Pottery Street, Greenock Inverclyde, PA15 2UZ. Works must be completed by 30 April 2027. The existing Greenock Police Station was built c. 1970 and is key in providing operational policing to the community of the Inverclyde area. Works must be completed by 30 April 2027. The existing Greenock Police Station was built c. 1970 and is key in providing operational policing to the community of the Inverclyde area. Over the past few decades, the use of the building has evolved, and alongside aspects due to general age of the building, and the roll out of various new systems, practices, and technologies, the current building no longer suits the requirements of 21st century policing. As such there is a need to exit the station and relocate the Police Station to another property at Ben Lomond View, Pottery Steet, Greenock. The intention is to refurbish Ben Lomond View, so it is fit for use for future years. The Authority is leasing the site from Riverside Inverclyde.

title: Scenario modelling to support development of a long term air quality policy framework for Scotland
description: 1. As part of wider work to develop a long term policy framework to replace the Scottish Governmentâs existing air quality strategy Cleaner Air for Scotland 2 (CAFS2), which expires at the end of 2026, air quality objectives in Scotland are being reviewed. Although all current objectives are being met across the country, an increasing body of research shows that air pollution, even at the low levels currently experienced in much of Scotland, continues to harm human health across all life stages and in a multitude of different ways. 2. The Scottish Governmentâs aim is to propose challenging but achievable new objectives, thereby delivering further benefits for human health. In the short term, we wish to assess the feasibility of matching or where possible going further than the air quality targets for nitrogen dioxide and fine particulate matter, two pollutants of concern for human health, which are set out in the EU Directive 2024/2881 on ambient air quality and cleaner air for Europe and are to be achieved by 2030. In the medium to longer term (i.e. the 10-15 years after 2030), we wish to consider the feasibility of going beyond the EU targets and working towards the considerably more stringent World Health Organisation guidelines, which were updated in 2021. Any proposals will be subject to public consultation and approval by Ministers prior to being adopted. 3. The project will require the successful tenderer to complete a range of survey, design and in-depth engagement work, including in-depth community, stakeholder and landowner engagement, topographic and utilities surveys, equality impact assessment (EqIA) and Preliminary Environmental Assessment (PEA) to ensure route(s) identified have strong community, neighbour and landowner support and that the design drawings for the route(s) are robust, deliverable and of a high quality. description: Market research has established that the technical requirements for these systems can only be met by Merrow Scientific Ltd, acting as the UK partner for Linseis MessgerÃ¤te GmbH. Both internal research activity and external customers require measurement across the full temperature range of â50Â°C to 1,000Â°C using xenon flash technology. Linseis is the only manufacturer identified that can deliver this range. The system can also achieve high vacuum levels at sub-ambient temperatures. This is particularly important for work down to â50Â°C, where it allows residual moisture to be effectively removed from the chamber. It also gives far greater control over the gas atmosphere surrounding the sample, supporting more consistent and reproducible measurement conditions. We recognise that closer engagement with communities, families, carers and the individuals that we support is required: focusing on the assets and strengths that individuals and their communities already have; to transform the way we all collaborate, maximising the opportunity for individuals to live independent lives and achieve their full potential. Connecting individuals with their communities is a key objective of maximising independence, and access to health and social care support, when needed, can improve health and wellbeing and support individuals to become more resilient. GCHSCP concluded a review of the access to social work services in 2024 to ensure our approach is fair and equitable for those eligible for services. The GCHSCP eligibility criteria will focus on those with substantial and critical need. description: Market research has established that the technical requirements for these systems can only be met by Merrow Scientific Ltd, acting as the UK partner for Linseis MessgerÃ¤te GmbH. Both internal research activity and external customers require measurement across the full temperature range of â50Â°C to 1,000Â°C using xenon flash technology. Linseis is the only manufacturer identified that can deliver this range. The system can also achieve high vacuum levels at sub-ambient temperatures. This is particularly important for work down to â50Â°C, where it allows residual moisture to be effectively removed from the chamber. It also gives far greater control over the gas atmosphere surrounding the sample, supporting more consistent and reproducible measurement conditions. The DSC offers very rapid heating rates and accurate heat capacity measurement, which is required to complement the LFA measurements. Its optical access allows the sample to be observed visually and opens the potential for spectroscopic analysis, such as Raman. This visual observation also strengthens the educational value of the technique. In addition, the DSC uses a replaceable chip, providing a cost-effective and sustainable means of maintaining reliable operation. This is critical for both the internal research community and external customers.
